title: Catching an exception: when a line can fail

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the hut desk here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Read a count of seats, or 0
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Counts` with a method `static int seats(String typed)`. It gives back the whole number in `typed`, with any spaces around it left out, and `0` when `typed` is not a whole number. It prints nothing. A `null` typed is a mistake in the calling code: its exception must reach the caller, so catch only the exception a text that is not a whole number brings.

Check calls `seats` with texts of its own: whole numbers, with and without spaces, a word, a number with a point, an empty text, and `null`. It reads what comes back, what is printed, and whether an exception reached it.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about try and catch, and about catching only what you expect.
Write the class and the first line of seats exactly as the task gives it.
Leave out the spaces, then read the number inside a try, with a catch for the one exception that brings.
Take the // off the first lines in main, and run the file with a number and with a word.
hints: The lesson shows the method that reads a whole number from a text, and the one that leaves out the spaces. Try them in main with " 12 " and with "twelve" to see which exception a word brings.
Only the line that reads the number belongs in the try. A null should fail outside it, or with an exception your catch does not name.
The shape: `String clean = typed.trim();`, then `try { return Integer.parseInt(clean); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { return 0; }`.

videos.title: Exception handling with try and catch

tasks.title: Add up the day, past the smudges
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Day` with a method `static String summary(String[] typed)`. It adds up the whole numbers in `typed`, each with any spaces around it left out, and counts the entries it could not read, as in `6 seats, 1 not read`. An entry that cannot be read never stops the others being added. A `null` in `typed` is a mistake in the calling code: its exception must reach the caller.

Check calls `summary` with entries of its own, a bad one first, in the middle or none at all, and one list with a `null` in it. It reads what comes back and whether an exception reached it.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about putting the try around only the line that can fail.
Write the class, the first line of summary, and two counts that start at 0.
Go through the entries with a loop, and decide where the try goes so one bad entry skips only itself.
Give back the text with both counts, and try it from main.
hints: When a line inside a try fails, everything after it in the try is skipped. Ask what a bad second entry should skip.
The try belongs inside the loop, around the reading of one entry; its catch counts that entry as not read, and the loop goes on.
Inside the loop: `String clean = entry.trim();`, then `try { seats += Integer.parseInt(clean); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { notRead++; }`.

tasks.title: Say who sits in a seat
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Seats` with a method `static String holder(String[] seats, String typed)`. `seats` holds a name for each seat, seat 1 first, and `typed` is a seat number as Bridie typed it. It gives back the name in that seat. When `typed` is not a whole number it gives back `Not a seat number: ` and what was typed. When the boat has no such seat it gives back `No such seat: ` and the message of the exception Java threw. A `null` seats is a mistake in the calling code: its exception must reach the caller.

Check calls `holder` with boats and seat numbers of its own, seat 0 and a seat past the last included, and with a `null` seats. It reads what comes back and whether an exception reached it.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about what a caught exception holds, and about two catches.
Try in main which exception a seat the boat does not have brings, and read its message.
Write holder with a catch for each of the two slips, each giving back its own text.
Try a good seat, a word and a seat too far from main.
hints: Two different slips throw two different exceptions, and each gets its own catch and its own answer.

Seat 1 is at position 0. A position the array does not have throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and the exception you catch holds the words the task wants after No such seat: the lesson shows how to read them.

One shape: `try { return seats[Integer.parseInt(typed) - 1]; } catch (NumberFormatException e) { return "Not a seat number: " + typed; } catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e) { return "No such seat: " + e.getMessage(); }`.
